quote: I already kind of, talked to a couple of solar companies. So to be honest, it really just comes down to, like, sending you my, PNM bill
stewart_read: Customer discloses he has already talked to competing solar companies and knows the space well, but the rep never asks which companies or what he was shown. That competitive intel would be free and useful for a closer, but it's never captured.
alternative_hypothesis: Rep may have judged that probing competitors would slow down a customer who is explicitly asking to move fast, making the omission a deliberate time-saving choice.
coaching_implication: Coach a 5-second version of the probe — 'which companies, quick?' — that doesn't derail the pace but captures competitive context for the next call.

quote: what if I cut the in person appointment and I all that sit down stuff? If I remove that and I set you up with just a phone call
stewart_read: The rep improvises a compromise (phone-only, no in-person) instead of using the canonical proposal-before-meeting rebuttal, which explains WHY the specialist walkthrough matters rather than just changing the delivery format.
alternative_hypothesis: This could be read as flexible customization rather than a violation, since the hard rule is about not sending the design unreviewed, and a phone call still satisfies that — but the rep never actually re-anchors on the reason a walkthrough matters, which weakens the pitch regardless of channel.
coaching_implication: Reinforce the WHY behind the no-email rule ('proposals require full explanation or they're confusing') so the rep leads with reasoning, not compromise offers, when this objection recurs.

quote: We're not gonna waste your time because I know we're one of the best. Like, you're you're gonna love our offer.
stewart_read: The rep responds to a customer who says he's solar-literate and comparison-shopping with generic superiority claims instead of creating curiosity about his specific numbers — a missed chance to say something like 'let's see what your actual bill shows' to pull him toward the appointment.
coaching_implication: Replay this moment — the rep had an opening to reference the customer's own PNM bill as the hook ('let's see what your bill actually shows before you compare') instead of a generic best-in-class claim.

quote: I can send you a picture of the panel that I currently have so then you guys can just give straight to the space.
stewart_read: Customer offers his own product-sourcing idea (send photos, get satellite imagery) — an engaged, solution-oriented moment — but the rep doesn't build on it or use it to steer toward booking the specialist call; he moves straight to a generic reassurance pitch instead.
alternative_hypothesis: The rep may have been holding this to fold into the same phone-appointment pitch he'd already offered at 01:35, rather than a separate miss — but no such follow-up reference occurs later in the call.
coaching_implication: Coach the rep to mirror back specifics the customer volunteers ('great, that's exactly the kind of info the specialist uses on the call') to make the appointment feel like the direct next step rather than a policy hurdle.

quote: To be real, brother, I don't wanna waste anybody's time. That's why I said via email.
stewart_read: This is a time/interest-style objection the rep could flip (e.g., reframing time-wasting as staying on his current bill rather than seeing his real numbers), but the rep responds with reassurance about the company's quality instead of an inversion.
coaching_implication: Use this as a live rep example to teach the inversion pattern — the customer handed him the exact language ('don't wanna waste time') to flip back onto the value of seeing the numbers.

quote: I want that just in an email. I don't I don't that's what I'm trying to tell you. If if you guys can't do it, then we can just end the call today
stewart_read: Third occurrence of the same email-only ask, now paired with an explicit exit threat. The rep's response at 03:57 restates policy rather than using the customer's own stated interest (wants a real price comparison) as leverage.
coaching_implication: This is the last chance to flip before the call ends — coach the rep to recognize repeated asks as an escalating signal requiring a different angle, not a repeated policy citation.

quote: Yeah. It's Bucky with Ion. I'm reaching out to oh, I'm reaching out about the solar form you filled online.
stewart_read: The intro references the form (partial legitimacy) but is delivered haltingly with a false start and no state or credibility anchor beyond the form reference — thinner than the standard template calls for.
alternative_hypothesis: The customer already knew who was calling ('Is this Daniel?') and answered before the rep even confirmed the reason for the call, suggesting some pre-existing context that may reduce the need for a full legitimacy build.
coaching_implication: Even on warm/expected calls, a clean one-breath intro sets a more confident tone than the halting delivery here — worth a quick rep note on pacing.
